summary: David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

David Zilberman (1938–1977) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under Yuri Levada (1968–1972). He held posts at Odesa University and Odessa Hydrometeorological Institute (1966), Hunter College (1973), the University of Chicago (1974), and Brandeis University (1976).

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh (1914–1989) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1943) under Walther Wüst (~1941–1943) and held posts at Alexandria University (~1953–1958) and Uppsala University (~1958–1979).
Daw Ohn (1913–2003) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics. She studied at the University of Rangoon, where she was later attested as Tutor in Pali in 1977.

Dawa Norbu (1949–2006) specialized in Tibetology and history. He studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi (~1969–1974), and UC Berkeley (1976–1982), later serving as professor for Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2006).

Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026). He held a post at Tibet University and taught Anna Sawerthal.
Dawei Wang works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sichuan University and held a post there at the Institute for Daoism and Religious Culture Studies.

Daya Krishna (1924–2007) was an Indian philosopher and Indologist. He served as professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under John Marshall. He held posts with the Archaeological Survey of India (1925, 1931–1935) and directed archaeological research in Jammu and Kashmir and Jaipur State (1935).

Dayananda Saraswati (1824–1883) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religion. He studied under Virajanand Dandeesha (~1860–1863), P. S. Subramania Iyer, Veeraraghavachariar, and several traditional teachers, and later taught scholars including Anantanand Rambachan and Michael Comans.

Dayong (1893–1929) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Bai Puren, and Dorje Geshe, taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute in 1923, and taught Fazun.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Dineschandra Sircar and served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1981–1983).
Debamitra Dey is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned both a BA Honours in Sanskrit (1997–2000) and a PhD (2003–2008) at Jadavpur University.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded and served as Director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages (~1969–1989) and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) was an Indian philosopher and Indologist who studied under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta at the University of Calcutta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1943) and served as visiting professor at Calcutta.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist who earned her PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar. She taught at UCLA (1978–1985) and held the chair of Asian art history at the University of Vienna (1994–2015).

Deborah Sutton is a historian and Indologist who earned her PhD in Modern History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (1997–2001). She holds a post as Professor in Modern South Asian History at Lancaster University (attested 2026).
Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching positions at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei (born 1968) is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China and served there as an associate professor of religious studies (attested 2005).

Deepro Chakraborty is an Indologist who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Alberta (PhD 2017). His teaching posts include St. Stephen's College (2014) and Gurudas College (2014–2017).
